characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-SEM equipped with EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors (Oxford); step size 120 nm and 250 nm on ~100×100 μm² and ~200×200 μm² areas; TSL-OIM software; samples polished to ~100 nm colloidal silica finish; three scans per sample
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn5Ni HR+CR is two-phase γ+B2; austenite deforms by planar slip (parallel slip bands) with mixed multi-coloured banded grains; phase map dominated by red FCC with sparse small blue B2 particles; no twinning or martensite.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cold-rolled (HR+CR) samples; IPF, image quality (IQ) and phase contrast maps
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine grain orientations, grain size, twin fractions, phase distribution (γ + B2), KAM and GOS

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku XRD instrument with Co-Kα radiation at 45 kV and 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: Supports identification of γ and B2 phases; used together with the Ni-alloy panels to track secondary-phase evolution.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Selected samples in HR+CR and heat-treated conditions
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases present in cold-rolled and heat-treated samples

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI TECNAI 20T G2 TEM operating at 200 kV equipped with EDAX EDS; twin-jet electropolished specimens (mixed acid, 243 K)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Resolved fine intragranular B2 (5–20 nm), intergranular B2 (50–200 nm) and κ-carbides in Ni-containing alloys.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases (κ-carbide, B2) at the nanoscale not resolvable by SEM-EBSD

characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn5Ni tensile specimens (HR+CR+1023 K) exhibited dimple morphology indicating ductile failure.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine fracture surfaces and failure modes

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AFFRI Vickers hardness tester, peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell 15 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness saturates to ~450 VHN at 50% cold reduction.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: As per ASTM E-140-02; averaged over ten measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness variation with cold work (and heat treatment)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Walter+Bai AG testing machine, constant cross-head speed 0.5 mm min^-1 (initial strain rate ~3 × 10^-4 s^-1)
characterization_methods.key_findings: HR+CR 28Mn5Ni: YS 1394 ± 5 MPa, UTS 1571 ± 5 MPa, TE 11 ± 0.4%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; flat specimens gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm; ASTM E8M; triplicated
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate strength and ductility in different processing conditions

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Irrespective of alloy content, austenite grains deformed mostly by planar slip, reflected by parallel slip bands (marked by an arrow in Fig. 1b). No deformation twinning or martensite transformation was observed in any cold-rolled alloy.

interfaces.interface_notes: γ/B2 phase boundaries exist in the two-phase 28Mn5Ni HR+CR microstructure.
interfaces.phase_evolution: B2 present already in the HR condition (prior stringers, ~4%); the 50% cold rolling step introduces no new precipitation.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip in austenite (parallel slip bands); no deformation twinning or martensite transformation.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: strength level and tensile elongation in HR+CR condition

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sound portion of the 30 kg vacuum-induction-melted ingot was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h.
Hot rolled at 1323 K to a final plate thickness of about 13 mm; this condition is denoted HR.

Samples cut from hot-rolled plates were cold rolled at room temperature in several passes to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets); denoted HR+CR. Reduction was capped at 50% for all alloys because 15Mn5Ni cracked beyond 50%.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: constant cross-head speed of 0.5 mm min^-1; tests triplicated and average reported
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat tensile specimen, gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm

tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: negligible strain hardening in HR+CR; strain hardening exponent n not reported for HR+CR (blank in Table 3)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s; values averaged over ten measurements

hardness.value: ~450 VHN (saturated value at 50% cold reduction for all three alloys)

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains (in prior HR state), heavily deformed by planar slip after cold rolling; banded/elongated with mixed colours in the IPF map
elongated stringers (bamboo-like) and polygonal particles; sparse small blue B2 particles in the phase-contrast map

precipitates.distribution: elongated stringers aligned with the deformation direction plus polygonal particles in the γ matrix
precipitates.type: B2 (Ni-rich ordered) prior stringers and polygonal particles

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase γ (FCC austenite) + B2 (ordered BCC) microstructure in the 50% cold-rolled (HR+CR) condition; austenite grains are heavily deformed, predominantly by planar slip (parallel slip bands), with no traces of deformation twinning or martensite transformation. B2 is present as prior stringers (bamboo-like) and polygonal/fine particles.

unmapped_findings: 28Mn5Ni (together with all three alloys) was cold rolled to ~50% reduction in thickness at room temperature without cracking; cold reduction was capped at 50% because 15Mn5Ni cracked beyond 50%.
In the HR+CR (50% cold reduction) condition the uniform strain (just before necking) was less than 3% for all three alloys, including 28Mn5Ni.

In the prior hot-rolled (HR) condition, 28Mn5Ni contained ~4% B2 phase (vs ~12% for 15Mn5Ni) in the form of elongated bamboo-like stringers and polygonal particles, with γ grain size ~5–7 μm and nearly random texture.
28Mn5Ni is reported to have higher austenite stability and lesser B2 precipitation, limiting carbon rejection around B2 relative to 15Mn5Ni.

In the HR+CR condition, the hardness and strength of all three alloys increased with degree of cold reduction at the expense of ductility, and all three converged to similar strength levels after 50% cold reduction (maximum work-hardening rate in the single-phase 28Mn0Ni alloy).
